title: THINGS THAT CAN BE DONE TO OR WITH A PATH

lists.name: THINGS THAT CAN BE DONE TO OR WITH A PATH
lists.of: action that can be done to or with a path
items: [Attract or be attracted to] [themselves, other paths, or other things].
[Be or become] [obstructed, opposed, confined, or otherwise restricted].
Change or transform [themselves, other paths, or other things].
[Circumnavigate, girdle, circumscribe, enclose, bound, outline, describe, measure, or orbit] things.
Combine with [<similar or different> paths, themselves, or other things] to form complex [systems, networks, or structures].
[Compete or struggle] with [one another or the environment].
Concentrate resources at [one point or a <series or system> of points].
[Connect, interconnect, unite, coordinate, or interact] [two or more] things.
[Detect and follow] the traces of former paths.
Distribute resources to [general or arbitrary] points (cf. 16).
[Feed or energize] [themselves, other paths, or other things].
Fill a [space or object] (e.g. a la a Peano curve that seems to [fill or constitute] a solid triangle).
[Grow, lengthen, or be added to <incrementally or from without>].
Hide only to later [reappear or regenerate].
Imitate [themselves, one another, or the environment].
IN COMBINATION WITH OTHER PATHS: keep many different [inputs, outputs, or flows] [separate or independent] of one another.
[Increase or maximize] the [efficiency or economy] of use of [space, materials, energies, or things]; or reduce needed [effort or attention].
Integrate [fluctuations, irregularities, randomness, spectrums, etc] [mathematically, physically, or mentally].
Mediate input or give [ingress or access].
Mediate output or allow [egress, escape, or disposal] (cf. 38).
[Overlap, superimpose, contain, or be contained in] other paths.
Pair with another path (perhaps involving antidirected movement).
Pass [over, around, or under] [themselves, other paths, or other things].
Project (e.g. a la a [vector, extrapolation, trajectory, or ray]).
[Pulsate, oscillate, wobble, weave, spiral, or corkscrew (helically)].
[Rationalize, systematize, fix, and/or routinize] [flow, movement, transport, travel, interaction, and/or exchange].
[Repel or escape from] [themselves, other paths, or other things] (cf. 6).
[Retreat, reverse, or double back on themselves] (cf. 3).
Supply a thing with something else.
[Tangle, wrap, or knot] [themselves, other paths, or other things].
[Tour, sample, or inspect] (or enable something to).
[Transmit <information, inquiries, or orders> or mediate control].

notes: List numbers omitted. Some brackets were unclosed or mismatched in the original and have been preserved or corrected according to visible legibility.
